papers.abstract: To develop a pathology-based preoperative decision-support system (Structured Imaging Report System for Pancreatic Cystic Lesions, SIRS-PCL) for subtype classification and risk stratification of PCLs. We conducted a multicentre retrospective study involving 1,102 patients treated between 1 January 2011 and 31 December 2024. The study cohort was divided into a development dataset (n = 858) and a temporal validation dataset (n = 244) from the periods 2011-2022 and 2023-2024, respectively. Three logistic prediction models were used to classify the five PCL subtypes and to perform separate three-tier risk stratifications (benign/low, medium, and high) for intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN) and mucinous cystic neoplasm (MCN) cases. SIRS-PCL was prospectively implemented at Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital from 25 June 2025 to 25 June 2026, and the diagnostic accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity were evaluated in a cohort of 76 patients. A total of 1,102 patients with PCLs were included in the study (median age 56 years, interquartile range 44-64), of whom 714 were female (64.8%). The five-category model included in SIRS-PCL achieved a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.93 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.91-0.95] in temporal validation. The IPMN model showed good discrimination for risk stratification (mean AUC 0.86, 95% CI 0.79-0.93), with the highest overall accuracy of 77.1% exceeding current guidelines (range 50.0%-58.6%). The MCN risk model also showed high performance (mean AUC 0.97, 95% CI 0.91-1.00). In comparison to current practice, SIRS-PCL use reduced unnecessary surgeries 11.5% vs. 23.1% and over-examinations 6.7% vs 33.7%. In the prospective implementation cohort, SIRS-PCL achieved accuracy of 86.2% for five-category pathological classification, 73.7% for IPMN risk stratification, and 100% for MCN risk stratification. SIRS-PCL is a pathology-based, quantitative decision-support system for preoperative pathological subtype classification and pathological risk stratification of surgically evaluated neoplastic PCLs.

papers.abstract: Renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibitors may influence cancer incidence, but previous findings have been inconsistent. We aimed to evaluate the associations of RAS inhibitor use with overall and site-specific cancer incidence. Participants receiving antihypertensive treatment without prior invasive cancer (except non-melanoma skin cancer) were identified from the UK Biobank. Individuals with missing covariate data were excluded. Participants were classified as ACEI users, ARB users, or RAS inhibitor non-users, defined as participants receiving antihypertensive medications other than ACEIs or ARBs. Outcomes included overall cancer incidence and site-specific cancers. Inverse probability of treatment-weighted Cox proportional hazards models were applied to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Among 94,696 participants followed for a mean of 11.5 years, 42,930 were ACEI users, 17,681 were ARB users, and 34,085 were RAS inhibitor non-users. No significant associations were observed between ACEI or ARB use and overall cancer incidence. In site-specific analyses, ARB use showed a modest association with higher prostate cancer incidence compared with ACEI use (HR = 0.90; 95% CI, 0.82-0.99) and RAS inhibitor non-use (HR = 1.14; 95% CI, 1.02-1.27). ACEI use was associated with lower bladder cancer incidence compared with RAS inhibitor non-use (HR = 0.71; 95% CI, 0.54-0.93). RAS inhibitor use was not associated with overall cancer incidence in this large cohort of antihypertensive medication users. Although modest associations were observed between ARB use and prostate cancer incidence and between ACEI use and bladder cancer incidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation in future studies.

papers.abstract: Prophylactic pelvic nodal radiotherapy (PRT) aims to eradicate occult pelvic nodal disease in oligometastatic prostate cancer but increases lymphocyte exposure. Its early hematologic safety and lymphocyte recovery when added to radiotherapy to the prostate/prostate region and all imaging-visible metastases remain uncertain. PROLONG2 is an ongoing, single-center, prospective, nonrandomized, two-arm cohort study. This interim analysis included 133 patients who completed radiotherapy: 86 with PRT and 47 without PRT (NPRT). The key safety endpoint was acute grade ≥ 3 lymphopenia. Other assessments included lymphocyte status at 6-12 months and acute hematologic and genitourinary/gastrointestinal toxicities. The association was estimated by multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, clinical N stage, and hormone-sensitivity status. Survival analysis was exploratory. Acute grade ≥ 3 lymphopenia occurred in 43/86 PRT patients (50.0%) and 8/47 NPRT patients (17.0%). PRT remained associated with acute grade ≥ 3 lymphopenia after adjustment (OR, 4.03; 95% CI, 1.55-11.54; p = 0.006). At 6-12 months, grade ≥ 2 lymphopenia occurred in 18.2% versus 16.7%, and grade ≥ 3 lymphopenia in 1.3% versus 2.4%, respectively. Among evaluable PRT patients with acute grade ≥ 3 lymphopenia, 25/38 (65.8%) recovered to grade 0-1. No acute grade ≥ 3 genitourinary/gastrointestinal toxicity occurred. Progression-free survival data remained immature, with only eight events reported. PRT was associated with markedly more acute lymphopenia, but persistent severe lymphopenia was uncommon and the between-group difference was substantially attenuated at 6-12 months. Continued prospective hematologic surveillance and mature survival data are needed to determine PRT's benefit-risk profile. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2400083776.

papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) typically arises within fibrotic, mechanically rigid microenvironments where matrix stiffness directly drives primary tumor proliferation and invasion. However, whether and how tumor cells retain these mechanical adaptations upon disseminating to softer metastatic sites has remained unclear. In this issue of Cancer Research, Luo and colleagues demonstrate that HCC cells retain a "mechanical memory" of matrix stiffness that persists even after metastasizing to soft secondary niches, such as the lungs. Mechanistically, this memory is mediated by contractility-dependent suppression of mitochondrial fission. The resulting accumulation of acetyl-CoA fuels sustained histone hyperacetylation, preserving a proliferative state across subsequent cell generations. These findings uncover a novel mechano-metabolic-epigenetic axis that sustains HCC proliferation during metastatic dissemination. See related article by Luo et al., p. 5354.

papers.abstract: Breast cancer progression reflects coupled immune and metabolic reprogramming, but biomarkers that capture this interplay and provide additional prognostic information beyond routine clinicopathological assessment remain limited. We developed an 11-gene immune-metabolic risk Score in TCGA-BRCA (n = 1099) by integrating C7 immune signatures and KEGG metabolic pathways through Cox and LASSO-Cox modeling. The fixed model was applied without retraining to three public cohorts and an independent institutional cohort of 146 patients from Harbin Medical University Cancer Hospital. The score consistently stratified overall survival across independent cohorts and provided additional prognostic information beyond conventional clinicopathological variables. Integrative analyses showed that high-risk tumors were characterized by enhanced cell-cycle and metabolic activation, reduced lymphocyte-associated immune features, and monocytic-lineage enrichment. At single-cell resolution, high-score cancer-associated fibroblasts exhibited enhanced extracellular-matrix remodeling, inflammatory iCAF activity, and TGF-β-associated immunosuppressive programs. In an exploratory pembrolizumab-containing cohort, lower pretreatment scores were associated with pathological complete response and immune-active transcriptional programs; however, these findings do not establish the score as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy benefit. The 11-gene immune-metabolic risk Score provides complementary prognostic stratification beyond conventional clinical variables and characterizes a stromal-remodeled immune-metabolic state associated with adverse breast cancer outcomes.

papers.abstract: Gemcitabine resistance remains a major therapeutic barrier in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), for which median survival in advanced disease has remained near one year despite extensive clinical investigation. Using artificial intelligence (AI)-guided structure-based drug repurposing, we identified sitagliptin, a DPP-4 inhibitor for diabetes, as a candidate ribonucleotide reductase (RRM1/2) inhibitor that sensitizes PDAC to gemcitabine. Molecular dynamics simulations suggested that sitagliptin disrupts gemcitabine-RRM1/2 interactions, downregulating RRM1/2 expression and restoring chemosensitivity across PDAC cell lines, patient-derived organoids, and mouse models. Sitagliptin enhanced the anti-tumor efficacy of both gemcitabine-nab-paclitaxel (GnP) and FOLFIRINOX regimens in preclinical studies. We conducted SITGEM-CARE, a single-center phase 2 trial in 22 patients with locally advanced or metastatic PDAC (median age 65.0 years; ECOG performance status 1, 86.4%; Stage IV, 68.2%; liver metastases, 54.5%). Patients received sitagliptin 100 mg orally once daily continuously, plus gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² and nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² on days 1 and 8 of 21-day cycles. Among 22 evaluable patients, eight achieved a partial response, and 11 had stable disease, yielding an objective response rate of 36.4% (95% CI: 17.2-59.3%) and a disease control rate of 86.4% (95% CI: 65.1-97.1%), with tumor shrinkage in 86.4% of patients. At a median follow-up of 9.9 months, the median progression-free survival was 6.6 months (95% CI: 4.8-12.4) with 6-month and 9-month PFS rates of 63.6% and 43.5%, respectively. Median overall survival was 12.5 months (95% CI: 7.8-not reached), with 62.9% of patients alive at 12 months. Furthermore, treatment was well tolerated, with no Grade 4/5 treatment-related adverse events. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in adequately powered, randomized trials. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05947825.

papers.abstract: Reversal of neuromuscular blockade (NMB) is a routine component of general anaesthesia with important implications for recovery quality and peri-operative safety. Recent changes in the cost of sugammadex, together with its efficacy and adverse effect profile relative to neostigmine, may influence its broader clinical use. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of sugammadex compared with neostigmine in adult patients. Systematic review of randomised controlled trials with meta-analyses and trial sequential analyses. Certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grades of Recommendation, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. This is an update of a 2017 Cochrane review. Online databases were searched up to December 2025. Randomised trials enrolling adults receiving rocuronium or vecuronium for elective procedures and comparing sugammadex with neostigmine were included. The outcomes included NMB recovery time and risk of various adverse events. We included 165 trials with 19 124 participants. Risk of bias was generally unclear or high. NMB monitoring technique was reported in 113 trials, mostly acceleromyography. Time to reversal of NMB from second twitch to a train-of-four ratio more than 0.9 was shorter with sugammadex 2 mg kg-1 versus neostigmine 0.05 mg kg-1 (mean difference = -10.49 min (95% confidence interval, -11.90 to -9.08), GRADE: moderate). Sugammadex probably reduces the number of patients with at least one adverse event compared with neostigmine (risk ratio = 0.72 (95% confidence interval, 0.61 to 0.84), GRADE: moderate). When looking at specific adverse events, sugammadex probably reduces the risk of residual NMB, inadequate NMB reversal, desaturation, atelectasis, increased upper airway secretion, airway obstruction, bradycardia, dry mouth and urinary retention (GRADE: moderate). Sugammadex probably reverses NMB more rapidly and with fewer adverse events than neostigmine. Broader use of sugammadex has the potential to improve peri-operative outcomes.

papers.abstract: Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with FGFR1 rearrangement (MLN-FGFR1) are rare, aggressive hematologic malignancies for which allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) remains the only potentially curative option. Pemigatinib, a reversible FGFR1-3 inhibitor, has substantial activity in chronic phase but lower efficacy in blast phase (BP). Data on futibatinib, an irreversible FGFR1-4 inhibitor, in BP MLN-FGFR1 are lacking. We report a 60-year-old man with MLN-ZMYM2::FGFR1 presenting in myeloid BP with extensive extramedullary disease (EMD) that was clinically refractory to induction chemotherapy. Initiation of off-label futibatinib was followed by rapid clinical improvement, complete cytogenetic remission (CCyR) and complete metabolic response (CMR), enabling bridging to allo-HCT from a mismatched unrelated donor. Futibatinib was subsequently continued as post-transplant maintenance with dose escalation and later combined with donor lymphocyte infusions (DLI). At last follow-up (day +497), the patient maintained a CMR and remained in CCyR with full donor chimerism, although ZMYM2::FGFR1 transcripts were still detectable at low levels in the bone marrow by droplet digital PCR. Next-generation sequencing additionally identified a germline DDX41 variant of uncertain significance, a finding potentially relevant to donor selection. To our knowledge, this is the first report of futibatinib used both as a bridge to transplantation and as post-transplant maintenance in BP MLN-FGFR1 with EMD. Although futibatinib's contribution cannot be separated from that of conditioning, graft-versus-leukemia activity and DLI, these hypothesis-generating findings provide support for further evaluation of irreversible FGFR1 inhibition in MLN-FGFR1.

papers.abstract: This prospective phase II XXX trial evaluated high-dose thoracic reirradiation for in-field recurrent lung cancer while respecting the cumulative dose to the organs at risk. Here, we report the toxicity and dosimetric results of the XXX trial. Patients with recurrent lung cancer within 5cm of the previously irradiated high-dose region (50Gy10 EQD2) were eligible. Patients were treated in a radical setting (≥45Gy10 EQD2) using conventionally (chemo)radiotherapy or stereotactic radiotherapy. Cumulative dose constraints were: tracheobronchial tree Dmax 110Gy3 EQD2, esophagus Dmax 100Gy3 EQD2 and spinal cord Dmax 75Gy3 EQD2. All doses were converted to EQD2 using α/β values of 10Gy (Gy10) for the tumor or acute effects and 3Gy for late effects (Gy3). Sixty patients were included. Thirty-eight patients were reirradiated with conventionally (chemo)radiotherapy most commonly 50Gy in 25 fractions or 60Gy in 30 fractions, while 22 patients received stereotactic radiotherapy most commonly 52.5Gy in 7 fractions. After a median follow-up of 26 months, no grade 4-5 toxicity was reported. Ten patients (17%) experienced grade 3 toxicity, including 7 cases of radiation pneumonitis. Dosimetric data were available for 59 patients. Median prescribed reirradiation dose was 60Gy10 EQD2, resulting in a median cumulative PTV Dmax of 130Gy10 EQD2. The cumulative esophagus dose exceeded 80Gy3 in 20 patients, cumulative trachea dose exceeded 80 Gy3 in 26 patients and cumulative bronchus dose exceeded 100Gy3 in 26 patients. Both cumulative lung V20 and cumulative mean lung dose were significantly associated with grade 2-3 radiation pneumonitis (p-value <0.05), whereas cumulative V5 was not. Thoracic reirradiation with a radical dose to the tumor while respecting cumulative organs at risk constraints was feasible in this prospective trial. Grade 2-3 radiation pneumonitis was associated with cumulative mean lung dose and cumulative lung V20. No grade 4-5 esophageal, airway or spinal cord toxicity occurred despite high cumulative doses.

papers.abstract: Though 100 kinase inhibitors are approved for clinical use, most kinases in the genome remain poorly characterized. Moreover, though kinase inhibitors have revolutionized the care of selected cancers, most others respond transiently or not at all to these drugs, typically directed against signal-transduction pathways. Given cellular regulation at every step by phosphorylation events, we hypothesized that phenotypic screening and machine-learning analysis can reveal novel kinase targets. Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), the most common lymphoma, responds poorly to signal transduction-directed kinase inhibitors. We applied a library of probes to DLBCL systems broadly representing its pathogenic heterogeneity and subjected results to iterative target-deconvolution analysis aimed at tumor selectivity (idTRAX). These efforts identified the cyclin G-associated kinase (GAK) as a tumor-selective target. Mechanistic studies showed GAK kinase activity is required for mitotic progression, with inhibition leading to G2/M arrest and cell death and increased efficacy in the absence of the retinoblastoma (RB) tumor suppressor. GAK-directed kinase inhibitors, including repurposed clinical compounds, showed promising single-agent anti-DLBCL activity in vivo. GAK kinase function is therefore a targetable dependency, opening novel treatment strategies suitable for rapid clinical translation. Moreover, we establish phenotypic screening with target deconvolution as a generalizable strategy to reveal tumor-selective kinase dependencies.

papers.abstract: Rectal gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) are rare, and their optimal surgical management remains controversial. This study compared clinicopathologic features and oncologic outcomes between total mesorectal excision (TME) and local excision (LE) to guide surgical strategy. We retrospectively analyzed 128 patients who underwent surgery for rectal GIST at Asan Medical Center between January 2000 and April 2023. Recurrence-free survival (RFS), overall survival (OS), and tumor downsizing were evaluated. Survival was measured from surgery or imatinib initiation in patients receiving neoadjuvant imatinib. Of 128 patients, 43(33.6%) underwent TME and 85(66.4%) underwent LE. Tumors > 5 cm and neoadjuvant imatinib use were more common with TME, whereas tumors < 2 cm and R0 resection were more frequent with LE. The 5-year RFS did not differ significantly between the LE and TME groups (98.8% vs. 92.6%, p = 0.184), whereas 5-year OS was higher after LE (96.8% vs. 92.1%, p = 0.047). Neoadjuvant imatinib reduced mean tumor diameter from 64.9 ± 23.5 mm to 49.2 ± 19.3 mm (p < 0.001). LE may provide acceptable recurrence control and potential functional advantages in selected patients. For large rectal GISTs, LE may be considered after adequate tumor downsizing with neoadjuvant imatinib.

papers.abstract: The optimal regimen for Hyperthermic IntraPEritoneal Chemotherapy (HIPEC) remains controversial. We aim to present long-term overall survival results from our phase 2 trial evaluating a concentration-based short-course regimen for ovarian cancer at the time of interval CytoReductive Surgery (iCRS). This was a multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 trial including patients with advanced ovarian cancer undergoing iCRS after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT). HIPEC was administered via the closed-abdomen technique for 30 min at 41°C-43°C, comprising the use of cisplatin (25 mg/L of perfusate/m2, total limit 240 mg) alone, or in combination with doxorubicin (15 mg/L, total limit 90 mg). Between February 2015 and July 2019, fifteen patients were enrolled and followed for a median of 110.6 months (95% CI, 85.2 - not reached). Median overall survival was 83.9 months (95% CI, 31.3 - not reached), with a 5-year survival rate of 53.3% (95% CI, 33.2-85.6) and a restricted mean survival time truncated at 5 years of 45·6 months (95% CI, 37.2-54.0). At the time of this analysis, 13.3% were alive without disease, 13.3% remained on systemic therapy, and 73.3% had died. Concentration-based short-course HIPEC is a feasible and safe regimen for ovarian cancer patients. This approach is associated with favorable long-term overall survival, highlighting the need for head-to-head comparisons of different HIPEC regimens.

papers.abstract: Wound-healing problems, both minor events and major wound-healing complications (WHCs), are common after soft tissue sarcoma (STS) surgery. Their impact on patient-reported recovery remains poorly defined. This study evaluated associations between postoperative WHCs and PROMIS physical and mental health outcomes. We performed a retrospective analysis of a prospectively collected, multi-institutional cohort of adults undergoing limb-sparing resection for extremity or trunk STS (2017-2025). Wound-healing events were recorded, and major WHCs were defined as complications requiring return to the operating room. PROMIS Global Physical Health and Global Mental Health T-scores were obtained preoperatively and at 3 and 6 months. Cross-sectional scores, change from baseline, and responder analyses (≥ 3-point improvement) were compared by WHC status. Of 74 patients, 45 (60.8%) experienced a wound-healing event and 16 (21.6%) developed a major WHC requiring reoperation. Baseline PROMIS scores were similar between groups. At 3 months, patients with wound-healing events had significantly worse physical and mental health recovery trajectories. Early events and reoperation were associated with worse physical function through 6 months. Postoperative wound-healing events, particularly early or major complications, are associated with clinically meaningful disruptions in patient-reported recovery, supporting the value of PROMIS-based postoperative monitoring.

papers.abstract: Many young women treated for gynecological cancer are assumed to experience long-term concerns about fertility and pregnancy, and psychological distress. However, evidence on patients' post-treatment reproductive concerns, decisions to pursue pregnancy, and oncofertility needs is limited. This study aims to provide insight into the perspectives of women treated with fertility-sparing surgery (FSS) for gynecological cancer and their partners. Women and their partners were selected for semi-structured interviews from our previously performed questionnaire study through purposive sampling based on self-reported reproductive concerns and pregnancy attempts. Interviews were coded and analyzed using a framework approach until data saturation was reached. Data saturation was achieved after 32 interviews with 24 participants and eight partners. Three participants did not pursue pregnancy and decided not to in the future. Participants expressed reproductive concerns and encounter post-treatment challenges, including a sense of time pressure, fear of cancer recurrence, and a common need for assisted reproductive techniques. Nearly all participants expressed their need for post-operative fertility counseling, although the preferred timing for this support varied. Partners considered their primary role as providing support throughout the treatment (decision) process, deciding to conceive and pursuing pregnancy. Some partners emphasized the importance, but lack of partner support. Women treated with FSS for gynecological cancer and their partners face persistent uncertainty regarding fertility and pregnancy, yet most women remain motivated to pursue pregnancy. Partners play a supportive role, but also have unmet needs. These findings highlight that reproductive issues should be systematically incorporated into routine clinical care pathways.

papers.abstract: Gastric cancer remains one of the most lethal malignant tumors worldwide. Whether selenium status before diagnosis is associated with survival following gastric cancer diagnosis remains unclear. Among 653 patients diagnosed with gastric cancer in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC) cohort, we examined associations of pre-diagnostic plasma selenium (Se), selenoprotein P (SELENOP) concentrations, and glutathione peroxidase 3 (GPX3) activity with gastric cancer-specific and overall mortality using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Blood samples were collected an average of 8.8 years before diagnosis. During follow-up, 483 patients died, including 359 from gastric cancer. The median observed time from diagnosis to death or censoring was 1.3 years. Multivariable-adjusted HRs (95% CIs) per one-SD increase in Se, SELENOP, and GPX3 were 0.95 (0.83-1.09), 0.94 (0.82-1.07), and 1.00 (0.88-1.14), respectively, for gastric cancer-specific mortality, and 0.97 (0.87-1.09), 0.94 (0.84-1.05), and 0.98 (0.87-1.09) for overall mortality. Pre-diagnostic biomarkers of selenium status were not clearly associated with gastric cancer-specific or overall mortality in this cohort. Further studies in populations with different selenium exposure distributions are needed to assess the generalizability of these findings and to replicate exploratory subgroup results.

papers.abstract: Cancer is a major cause of morbidity and mortality among people with HIV (PWH). We assessed temporal trends in five-year mortality and compared recent cancer survival with standardized Italian general-population estimates. We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study including adult PWH diagnosed with malignancy at Luigi Sacco Hospital, Milan, between 2000 and 2020. Cancers were classified as AIDS-defining cancers (ADCs), virus-related non-AIDS-defining cancers (NADCs), and non-virus-related NADCs. Five-year all-cause and cancer-related mortality were compared between 2000-2007 and 2008-2020 using survival estimates and adjusted Cox models. For selected cancers diagnosed in 2008-2020, five-year net survival was estimated using the Ederer II method and descriptively compared with standardized Italian estimates. Overall, 476 malignancies were diagnosed, including 200 ADCs and 276 NADCs. Five-year all-cause mortality decreased from 39.3% to 15.7% for ADCs (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.39, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.20-0.74; p = 0.004), from 56.4% to 31.1% for virus-related NADCs (aHR 0.34, 95% CI 0.16-0.71; p = 0.004), and from 58.8% to 44.3% for non-virus-related NADCs (aHR 0.55, 95% CI 0.32-0.94; p = 0.029). Five-year net survival in PWH was 30% for lung cancer, 60% for liver cancer, 83% for anal cancer, 71% for non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and 95% for Kaposi sarcoma. Corresponding standardized general-population estimates were 24%, 31%, 70%, 80%, and 84%, respectively. Five-year mortality among PWH with cancer improved substantially over time, particularly for ADCs and virus-related NADCs. Net survival point estimates were numerically higher than standardized references for liver and anal cancer, broadly similar for lung cancer, and lower for non-Hodgkin lymphoma; the Kaposi sarcoma reference was historical (2005-2009). Persistently high mortality among PWH with non-virus-related cancers underscores the need to strengthen prevention, early diagnosis, and access to appropriate oncological care.

papers.abstract: Gastric cancer incidence declined markedly during the twentieth century in the United States, and birth-cohort patterns are recognized. Whether the rate of decline changed across generations, and when, is less characterized. We examined Connecticut birth cohorts to identify changes in the tempo of decline and assess their timing against etiologic and environmental explanations. We analyzed 17,958 gastric cancers recorded in the Connecticut Tumor Registry (1935-1979). Birth-cohort analyses included 16,148 cases aged 45-84 years and were conducted separately by sex using age-period-cohort and segmented models. Robustness was assessed by excluding early registry periods, age groups, and calendar periods. Historical public-health, typhoid mortality, and refrigeration data characterized environmental changes. Among men, the cohort decline accelerated around the 1885 birth cohort (likelihood-ratio χ² = 87.5). The breakpoint remained near 1885 after exclusion of early registry periods, seven of eight age groups, and each of nine calendar periods. Among women, the best-fitting candidate breakpoint was 1865, but improvement over the single-slope model was smaller (likelihood-ratio χ² = 9.9), and the breakpoint was less stable across age-group exclusions. The male transition coincided with sanitary changes and declining typhoid mortality but preceded widespread household mechanical refrigeration by decades. By identifying a change within an established generational decline, these findings localize a robust acceleration in male gastric cancer decline to generations born around 1885. Although temporal correspondence cannot establish causation, the timing supports a life-course interpretation in which changing childhood environments, potentially affecting Helicobacter pylori acquisition, contributed to gastric cancer declines.

papers.abstract: Constitutional mismatch repair deficiency syndrome (CMMRD) syndrome, caused by inherited biallelic mismatch repair (MMR) gene loss, is characterized by early-onset cancers and neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) features. Genetic heterogeneity of syndromes with replication repair deficiency (RRD) and non-RRD conditions (eg, Lynch syndrome (LS) and NF1, respectively) leads to diagnostic challenges. Seven diagnostic criteria (CMMRD1-CMMRD7) were established in 2022 incorporating germline results, ancillary tests, and clinical manifestation. This study reviews the use of these criteria in identifying CMMRD. Individuals suspected of CMMRD referred to the International Replication Repair Deficiency Consortium in Toronto, Canada, had clinical manifestation, family history, germline, MMR immunohistochemistry (IHC) of non-neoplastic (NN-IHC) and tumor tissue, and LOGIC obtained to assess the diagnostic criteria. A total of 580 individuals were identified, with 159 excluded because of insufficient information resulting in 421 individuals assessed using the diagnostic criteria. Of these, 358 (85%) were classified as CMMRD/suspected CMMRD (n = 270), LS/likely LS (n = 78), or other hereditary conditions (n = 10). Sixty-three individuals could not be classified because of the lack of or discordant results. Of the 270 patients with CMMRD syndrome, 241 met the published criteria and 29 were suspected of CMMRD on the basis of fulfilling criteria with a discordant functional result or suspicious genotype/phenotype. CMMRD1-CMMRD7 criteria were all identified, with 57% (n = 137) fulfilling CMMRD1 criteria. Early-onset gliomas and GI cancers occurred in LS, POLE, TP53, and NF1. Digenic LS and concurrent hereditary cancer syndromes were identified. The 2022 CMMRD syndrome diagnostic criteria provided a useful framework for establishing CMMRD syndrome and distinguishing it from similar conditions. A clinically meaningful subset remained difficult to classify despite suspicion of CMMRD. Refinement of CMMRD syndrome diagnostic criteria may address atypical presentation and discordant functional results. Limitations include incomplete availability of germline/functional testing, discordant/inconclusive results, and inherent referral bias to a specialized RRD consortium.

papers.abstract: Chemotherapy remains the backbone of neoadjuvant treatment for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), and response to chemotherapy strongly correlates with patient prognosis. However, predicting chemoresistance remains a major clinical challenge. To address this obstacle, we performed serial fine needle aspirations followed by RNA-sequencing on patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models of TNBC that were either chemoresponsive or chemoresistant. We found that these two classes of PDX models exhibited distinct transcriptional trajectories that diverged within one week of chemotherapy initiation, preceding measurable changes in tumor volume. At early time points, chemoresponsive tumors showed activation of apoptotic and cytokine-related pathways, while these changes were absent in chemoresistant models. Notably, cytokine upregulation in chemoresponsive tumors coincided with infiltration of myeloid-derived immune cells into the tumor bed within seven days of chemotherapy, indicating active microenvironment remodeling, even in mice lacking a fully intact immune system. Analysis of paired biopsies from patients with TNBC collected before treatment and within four days of the first chemotherapy dose revealed a consistent pattern: chemoresponsive tumors upregulated inflammatory pathways, whereas chemoresistant tumors showed diminished activation of these pathways. These results underscore the potential clinical value of early on-treatment tumor sampling to detect chemoresistance and guide therapeutic intervention.

papers.abstract: KRAS is the most frequently mutated oncogene in pancreatic cancer, with over 90% of patients harboring KRAS mutations, approximately 45% of which are G12D substitutions. The development of KRASG12D selective inhibitors, such as HRS-4642, MRTX1133 and RMC-9805, has brought new hope for treating this patient population. However, the clinical efficacy of these inhibitors is limited by the emergence of acquired resistance, the mechanisms of which remain incompletely understood. Our study employed a KRAS saturation mutagenesis library to systematically map the landscape of KRAS mutations conferring resistance to HRS-4642 and MRTX1133. We identified several secondary mutations-including R73P, E63P, D69W, and M72K-that confer resistance to both inhibitors, while M72H was found specifically resistant to HRS-4642. We further characterized the impact of these mutations on KRAS downstream signaling and performed structural modeling of the mutant proteins. Through molecular dynamics simulations, we suggested that the R73P mutation, although distant from the binding pocket, is predicted to exert a global dynamic effect on the allosteric site, thereby disrupting inhibitor-protein interactions. This suggests the existence of a novel class of KRAS resistance mutations and a previously unrecognized mechanism of acquired resistance to KRAS-targeted therapies. Furthermore, we identified Y64W, A59G, and R73P as mutations that concurrently confer resistance to the tri-complex inhibitor RMC-9805, as well as to the allosteric inhibitors MRTX1133 and HRS-4642. This comprehensive analysis delineates the global landscape of secondary resistance mutations to KRASG12D-selective inhibitors.

papers.abstract: The coexistence of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung cancer (LC) presents a complex clinical scenario with distinct pathological interactions. Beyond shared epidemiological and genetic risk factors, COPD reshapes the pulmonary immune microenvironment through reprogrammed immune-cell compartments, aberrant programmed cell death, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), fostering an immunologically "hot" but pathologically permissive milieu that simultaneously drives carcinogenesis and influences treatment responsiveness. Recent evidence suggests that COPD may confer an altered immunological microenvironment that paradoxically enhances responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in patients with LC. This review mainly synthesizes clinical evidence on the efficacy of ICI, currently the most widely used immunotherapy, in LC patients concomitant with COPD and elucidates potential immunological and molecular mechanisms underlying observed clinical benefits, including heightened programmed cell death protein ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression, elevated tumor mutational burden, increased human leukocyte antigen I (HLA-I) expression, enriched tissue-resident memory T cells and mucosal-associated invariant T cells, and a macrophage polarization shift toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype, with benefits appearing largely attributable to patients with mild-to-moderate airflow obstruction. The safety profile of ICIs in this population-exacerbation risk, eosinophilic airway disease, checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP), and autoimmune thyroiditis-is appraised, alongside emerging strategies such as lymphocyte-activation gene 3 (LAG-3), T-cell immunoglobulin and mucin-domain containing-3 (TIM-3), and T cell immunoreceptor with Ig and ITIM domains (TIGIT) blockade and the immunomodulatory potential of COPD medications (inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting β-agonists). Current evidence remains limited by small retrospective cohorts and heterogeneous stratification. Large-scale prospective studies are warranted. This review aims to clarify the prognostic value of concomitant COPD and guide precision therapeutic strategies for this growing comorbid population.

papers.abstract: Although human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (ERBB2/HER2) is a validated therapeutic target, the significance of ERBB3 (HER3) alterations across solid tumours remains poorly defined. We characterised such alterations to clarify the genomic landscape relevant to HER3-directed strategies, distinguishing somatic events from germline polymorphisms. We analysed real-world data from 5416 patients with metastatic solid tumours who underwent next-generation sequencing. As tumour-only sequencing cannot separate germline from somatic variants, recurrent germline-pattern variants were reclassified using gnomAD and Korean population databases, and remaining somatic variants were annotated for oncogenicity using OncoKB (v7.3, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, New York, NY). Overall survival (OS) was analysed via Cox regression analysis stratified according to tumour type. ERBB3 alterations were initially identified in 12.9% of patients, dominated by mutations (12.3%) rather than amplifications (0.8%). However, the two most common variants, K498I and R1127H, proved to be common germline polymorphisms, and germline-pattern variants accounted for 63% of all mutation calls. After germline exclusion, the prevalence of somatic mutations was 4.5%, and oncogenic/likely-oncogenic mutations only 1.6%, matching a large pan-cancer series. Oncogenic mutations clustered in extracellular domains, were tumour-type-specific (V104M/L in colorectal and urothelial; G284R in gastric and biliary tract cancer), and persisted in nonhypermutated tumours. The ERBB3 mutation status was not prognostic (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.97, P = 0.52), whereas ERBB3 amplification was independently associated with a worse OS (HR 1.43, P = 0.024). Most apparent ERBB3 mutations in this East Asian tumour-only cohort were likely germline polymorphisms; true somatic oncogenic mutations were uncommon and tumour-type-specific, whereas amplification was rare but prognostically adverse. As HER3-directed antibody-drug conjugates depend on HER3 protein expression, the integration of such data with HER3 immunohistochemistry and outcomes is essential to define the target population.

papers.abstract: Magrolimab blocks CD47, a molecule that mediates cancer immune evasion from phagocytes. The ELEVATE TNBC study evaluated magrolimab plus standard-of-care therapies in advanced/metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (mTNBC). Two cohorts were enrolled in the safety run-in (SRI) and phase II portions. Phase II cohort 1 randomly assigned 28 patients with untreated, programmed death-ligand 1-negative mTNBC to receive nab-paclitaxel or paclitaxel with/without magrolimab. Phase II cohort 2 enrolled 43 patients with mTNBC (one to two prior lines of treatment in the metastatic setting) to receive magrolimab with sacituzumab govitecan. Primary endpoints were adverse event (AE) incidence (SRIs), investigator-assessed progression-free survival (PFS; phase II cohort 1), and objective response rate (ORR; phase II cohort 2). No dose-limiting toxicities occurred. In phase II cohort 1, median PFS was 13.9 and 10.0 months (hazard ratio 0.456, 95% confidence interval 0.147-1.409) and ORRs were 35.7% and 21.4% for magrolimab-taxane and taxane therapy, respectively. In phase II cohort 2, ORR was 38.1%, and median PFS was 5.5 months. Early study closure limited interpretation of efficacy; PFS/ORR values should be considered descriptive. AE rates were consistent with known profiles for each agent, with no new safety signals or fatal AEs. Magrolimab plus standard of care was manageable. Further studies are needed to determine the role of anti-CD47 therapies in mTNBC.

papers.abstract: Although highly preventable, cervical cancer remains one of the most common malignancies among women worldwide. As part of the Global Burden of Disease study, we estimated cervical cancer incidence, mortality and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts to 2050. In 2023, 887,000 new cases (95% uncertainty interval 682,000-1,170,000), 369,000 deaths (292,000-475,000) and 13.3 million DALYs (10.1-17.4) were estimated globally. Age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) and age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR) were more than four and seven times higher in low- versus high-income countries. Between 1990 and 2023, global ASIR was largely stable (-0.4% (-26.6 to 34.7)), whereas ASMR changed by -17.5% (-36.2 to 13.4). All cervical cancer DALYs were attributable to human papillomavirus infection, with tobacco use contributing 5.9% (3.2-9.3) globally. By 2050, global ASIR and ASMR are forecast to change by -12.5% (-25.7 to 3.5) and -9.0% (-21.5 to 6.6) from 2024, yet absolute cases and deaths are forecast to rise by 20.2% (4.6-38.5) and 39.3% (23.6-57.3). ASIR and ASMR are forecast to remain highest in low-income countries. Intensified action is needed to accelerate progress.

papers.abstract: Susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia is generally considered to follow an autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with incomplete penetrance. In a recent study in the British Journal of Anaesthesia, Aboelsaod and colleagues integrate national epidemiological data, anaesthetic exposure histories, population genomics, contracture test phenotyping, and Bayesian modelling to estimate the prevalence of individuals capable of developing clinical malignant hyperthermia. Their findings support a threshold model in which variants contribute different degrees of biological liability, potentially modified by other genetic and environmental factors, whereas the probability of reacting during a triggering exposure seems relatively similar once an individual has crossed this threshold. The study also illustrates how combining complementary sources of imperfect evidence can improve risk estimation for rare, exposure-dependent disorders. Ultimately, malignant hyperthermia genetics needs to move beyond categorical variant classification towards variant-specific penetrance estimates that incorporate genetic background, ancestry, exposure history, and other determinants of clinical expression.

papers.abstract: There is an urgent global need for affordable, large-scale health screening to enhance preventive care in the ageing population. Using low-cost, non-invasive retinal photographs and leveraging large foundation models, we developed a deep learning-based biomarker, Retinal Mortality Equivalent (RetiME), that directly mapped retinal features to individual mortality risk. Trained on a European cohort and externally validated across three independent external cohorts spanning Southeast Asia, Eurasia and North America, RetiME showed robust associations with all-cause and cause-specific mortality and predicted the incidence of a wide range of systemic and ocular diseases. Crucially, beyond static risk estimation, RetiME re-timed mortality risk by reconstructing personalized lifespan trajectories that were associated with observed mortality outcomes (for example, age of death). Clustering of these trajectories revealed distinct mortality patterns, spanning cancer-predominant, cardiometabolic and neurodegenerative risks, reflecting diverse ageing pathways captured by RetiME. Interpretability analyses showed that RetiME captures diverse biological and retinal features underlying mortality risk. Genome-wide analyses further identified genetic loci associated with RetiME. Collectively, these findings support further evaluation of retinal imaging and trajectory modelling as one component of a comprehensive assessment of mortality risk.

papers.abstract: CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy (CAR19) improves survival in relapsed/refractory large B cell lymphoma compared with immunochemotherapy with intent for autologous hematopoietic cell transplantation (autoHCT). However, major toxicities include prolonged cytopenias, infection and secondary hematologic malignancies. Here, to investigate these complications, we studied patients with lymphoma receiving CAR19 and compared clinical outcomes to propensity-matched autoHCT-treated controls. CAR19-treated patients exhibited impaired immune reconstitution and increased infection. Bone marrow analysis showed that prolonged post-CAR cytopenias are associated with clonal cytopenias of undetermined significance and interferon-mediated inflammation. Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) commonly expanded following CAR19 infusion and was associated with impaired immune reconstitution and treatment-related myeloid malignancy (tMN). Post-CAR tMN was molecularly and clinically comparable to post-autoHCT tMN. Single-cell DNA analysis revealed mostly independent CH clones, while CAR integration into CH-mutant T cells occurred frequently and may drive expansion and persistence. Together, these findings implicate CH expansion and marrow inflammation in key CAR19-associated toxicities.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by inflammatory signaling and metabolic adaptation within the tumor microenvironment. We integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets to characterize inflammation-associated metabolic programs in PDAC. Three public PDAC datasets were analyzed: TCGA-PAAD bulk RNA-seq data, GSE62452 tumor and adjacent tissue microarray data, and GSE154778 single-cell RNA-seq data from primary and metastatic PDAC. Kynurenine-, arachidonic acid-, inflammasome-, and glutamine-related transcriptional modules were evaluated. Cell-based qRT-PCR was used to validate selected inflammatory-metabolic genes after 48 h of cytokine stimulation. In GSE62452, 5985 of 33,297 probes were differentially expressed between tumor and adjacent tissues, including 3701 increased and 2284 decreased probes. Among selected targets, KYNU showed the largest increase. In 60 matched pairs, IDO1, KYNU, PTGS2, and PLA2G4A were significantly elevated in tumor tissues. Analysis of 14,926 single cells showed that myeloid cells had the highest mean scores across all four inflammatory-metabolic modules. Bulk expression patterns were positively associated across datasets (Spearman ρ=0.745, P = 0.0133). qRT-PCR further demonstrated cytokine-induced expression of selected inflammatory-metabolic genes. Integrated bulk and single-cell analyses identify inflammation-associated metabolic transcriptional programs in PDAC, with prominent activity in myeloid cells. These findings provide a transcriptomic framework for future mechanistic and multi-omic validation rather than direct evidence of metabolic flux or clinical utility.

papers.abstract: In resected liver-limited metastatic colorectal cancer (LL-mCRC), disease-free survival (DFS) and postsurgical overall survival (psOS) have been found to be weakly related in heterogeneous retrospective series, challenging the role of DFS as a surrogate biomarker of psOS. Additionally, it remains unclear whether early relapses (DFS <6 months) are associated with overall survival (OS) benefit. We analyzed individual data of patients with LL-mCRC enrolled in nine randomized trials of first-line chemotherapy plus biologics. Correlation and surrogacy between DFS and psOS were calculated with ρ and R2. psOS of resected patients with DFS <6 months was compared with time from minimum disease load (post-min OS) of unresected patients, with stratification according to baseline tumor burden score (TBS). Time on systemic therapy was also evaluated. Eight hundred fifty-five patients with LL-mCRC were included and 357 (42%) were radically resected. DFS and psOS were highly correlated (ρ = 0.73), with R2 at the patient and trial levels for surrogacy of 0.70 and 0.32, respectively. psOS and post-min OS in resected patients with early relapse (n= 115) and unresected patients (n = 498) were comparable [hazard ratio (HR) 0.88, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.70-1.11, P = 0.29]. However, a benefit from surgery was detected in patients with high baseline TBS (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.45-1.05, P = 0.09) but not in patients with low/medium baseline TBS (HR 1.12, 95% CI 0.74-1.69, P = 0.59) (p interaction = 0.10). Resection was associated with a lower percentage of time on systemic therapy (26%) regardless of DFS (47% if <6 months, 26% if ≥6 months) (P < 0.001). In LL-mCRC resected after first-line chemotherapy plus biologics, DFS is highly correlated with psOS, with high patient-level surrogacy. In high-burden patients, liver surgery seems associated with a trend toward long-term benefit, also after early relapse (<6 months), whereas time on systemic therapy is reduced.

papers.abstract: We aimed to assess the public perception of who is responsible for anesthesia-related hospital care tasks in Japan and examine associated factors. We conducted a cross-sectional, nationwide, quota-based web survey of adults in Japan in July 2025. Of the 1,944 respondents who initiated the survey, 1,844 completed (94.9%) it, and 1,000 responses were analyzed after quota completion (ages 20-69 yr). The outcomes were attribution (yes/no) of four anesthesia-related hospital care tasks to anesthesiologists: intraoperative anesthesia, postoperative pain management, procedural sedation/analgesia (PSA), and labour neuraxial analgesia (LNA). For each outcome, we fitted multivariable logistic regression models adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics, the Health Interest Scale (HIS), Communicative and Critical Health Literacy (CCHL), board-certified anesthesiologist density, information sources, and task-matched experience, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) control. Attribution was highest for intraoperative anesthesia (84.7%), followed by LNA (65.2%), PSA (37.4%), and postoperative pain management (13.5%). After FDR control, university education or higher was associated with greater attribution for intraoperative anesthesia (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.08; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.30 to 3.32), PSA (aOR, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.15 to 2.30), and LNA (aOR, 1.82; 95% CI, 1.30 to 2.55). Task-matched prior experience attributed to anesthesiologists was associated with higher attribution for intraoperative anesthesia (aOR, 3.75; 95% CI, 1.76 to 8.80) and PSA (aOR, 2.41; 95% CI, 1.34 to 4.43). Fictional media was the only information-source factor that remained significant after FDR control (intraoperative anesthesia: aOR, 2.73; 95% CI, 1.79 to 4.25; PSA: aOR, 1.90; 95% CI, 1.42 to 2.56). No factor met the FDR threshold for postoperative pain management. HIS, CCHL, and anesthesiologist density showed no consistent adjusted associations. Public attribution of anesthesiologists' roles in Japan varied by task. Educational attainment, task-matched experience, and information sources were more consistently associated with attribution than general health traits or workforce context, supporting the value of role-explicit, task-specific communication strategies.

papers.abstract: Cancer is a growing health and economic burden worldwide, yet comprehensive global estimates of cancer treatment costs are sparse. Such data are crucial for economic evaluations to inform policy making and practice to improve cancer control and outcomes. We aimed to synthesise available estimates of direct cancer treatment costs by stage, year, and follow-up period and predict global cancer treatment costs. In this systematic review and modelling study, we extracted estimates of cancer treatment costs (ie, direct treatment costs only) from the medical literature, screening 25 896 studies, of which 196 were included in our final dataset, covering 31 cancer types across 44 countries. Costs were standardised as a ratio of country GDP per capita and adjusted for follow-up period. We used a Bayesian hierarchical model to synthesise the estimates as a function of GDP per capita, accounting for cancer type, stage (I-IV), year of diagnosis, and follow-up period. We then estimated global and regional treatment costs (overall and by cancer type) in US$ 2022 based on the latest available incidence data from GLOBOCAN. This study is registered on PROSPERO (#CRD420251138446). Globally, total 10-year treatment costs for newly diagnosed cancers in 2022 were estimated to be $771·48 billion (95% UI 719·99-823·81), with breast cancer being the largest driver of costs ($96·07 billion [80·78-109·43]), followed by leukaemia ($86·11 billion [80·36-94·87]) and lung cancer ($84·36 billion [73·18-95·28]). North America and Europe accounted for 64% of total costs, but only 36% of diagnosed cancer cases. Mean costs per diagnosed patient were $38 650 (95% UI 36 070-41 280) globally, ranging from $3380 (95% UI 2960-3820) in eastern Africa to $93 600 (95% UI 87 170-100 150) in North America. As a ratio of GDP per capita, treatment costs declined with increasing GDP per capita (from 3·16 [95% UI 2·61-3·81] at $500 GDP per capita to 1·36 [1·07-1·70] at $100 000 GDP per capita), especially for stage IV cancers, which declined from 8·06 (6·57-9·61) at $500 GDP per capita to 4·53 (3·48-5·83) at $100 000 GDP per capita. Cancer types with the highest mean cost ratios were bone cancer (6·27 [95% UI 2·45-11·73]), leukaemia (6·16 [5·59-7·01]), and multiple myeloma (5·74 [3·78-6·74]). Treatment costs remained stable over time by year of diagnosis for stage I-II cancers, but steadily increased for stage III cancers, and rose substantially for stage IV cancers. These cost estimates provide new important data for economic evaluations, which can support expenditure planning, priority setting, and policy making to help guide strategic investment and resource allocations to improve cancer care and outcomes across different settings. papers.abstract: Pulmonary aspiration of gastric contents remains an important cause of anaesthetic morbidity and mortality, and is important medicolegally. Rapid sequence induction is a multi-element technique designed to mitigate risk in those patients at increased risk of pulmonary aspiration during induction of general anaesthesia. We undertook a narrative review to summarise evidence and evidence gaps focusing on controversial aspects of rapid sequence induction. Despite widespread use of rapid sequence induction, many elements of the technique lack robust evidence and consensus. Nasogastric tubes can be used to reduce gastric content, but do not empty the stomach reliably. Correctly applied cricoid force obstructs the hypopharynx and has a limited impact on airway management, but incorrect application can cause clinically significant difficulties. Correct location of cricoid force may require ultrasound localisation of the cricoid cartilage. Applying the correct force, which varies with age and sex, is improved by education, practice and feedback. The use of videolaryngoscopy during rapid sequence induction is supported by evidence. The role of gastric ultrasound in determining anaesthetic technique is uncertain. Cardiovascular complications of rapid sequence induction are common, particularly in the patients who are critically ill, and modifications to the technique may reduce their frequency and severity. Effective use of airway rescue techniques may require removal of cricoid force. There is insufficient evidence for many of the elements of rapid sequence induction to determine whether they reduce patient harm or to state confidently that they do not. Controversies and evidence gaps should be acknowledged. Despite this, optimal use of rapid sequence induction requires a thorough knowledge of the subject, including areas of uncertainty to guide individualised risk assessment; clinical decision-making; and practical conduct of the technique.

papers.abstract: Preoperative immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are active in patients with deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) colon cancer (CC), whereas proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) CC has been consistently considered resistant to first-generation ICIs. In the phase 2 UNICORN trial, we evaluated short-course preoperative botensilimab (BOT; multifunctional Fc-enhanced anti-CTLA-4 monoclonal antibody) alone or in combination with the anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody balstilimab (BOT + BAL) in 56 patients with resectable, locally advanced CC. Twenty-eight patients with pMMR CC were sequentially enrolled in BOT (n = 14) and BOT + BAL (n = 14) cohorts. Twenty-eight patients with dMMR CC followed the same sequential allocation strategy. The primary endpoint of centrally assessed pathological major response (pMR) rate (≤10% of residual viable tumor) was met in all cohorts, except pMMR BOT. Specifically, the pMR rate was 0% (95% confidence interval (CI): 0-23.2%) in pMMR BOT, 36% (95% CI: 12.8-64.9%) in pMMR BOT + BAL, 36% (95% CI: 12.8-64.9%) in dMMR BOT and 100% (95% CI: 76.8-100%) in dMMR BOT + BAL. Secondary endpoints included safety, quality of life, describing treatment-induced transcriptional dynamics, peripheral blood mononuclear cell dynamics, radiomics and radiogenomics features, fecal microbiota composition and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) dynamics. Eight (29%) and 15 (54%) patients treated with BOT and BOT + BAL, respectively, experienced immune-related adverse events, most commonly flu-like syndrome and diarrhea. Single-cell spatial transcriptomic analysis of matched baseline and post-treatment samples highlighted high baseline PD-L1 stromal expression and low post-treatment regulatory T cell signatures in pMMR responders, whereas dMMR responders displayed high baseline FCGR2A and FCGR3A expression on intratumoral macrophages. Clearance of ctDNA before surgery correlated with pathological response and lack of recurrence at data cutoff. Preoperative BOT + BAL elicits pathological responses in patients with pMMR or dMMR CC, supporting the combination as a promising strategy to expand ICI benefits to the early-stage setting. papers.abstract: The Delphi methodology is a widely-used tool for achieving expert consensus in healthcare, particularly in areas where empirical evidence is limited or uncertain. Despite its structured design, the Delphi process remains vulnerable to implicit cognitive biases that may influence judgement and group decision-making. Such biases may inadvertently affect the quality of the consensus process, allow louder voices to influence outcomes, restrict inclusivity and undermine the validity, transparency and evidence-based nature of recommendations. We conducted a methodological review synthesising literature from cognitive psychology, behavioural science and methodological research on consensus development and Delphi processes. Using a concept-mapping approach, established cognitive biases were mapped to different stages of the Delphi process, including study design; panel selection; survey development; iterative scoring; and consensus interpretation. Ten cognitive biases were organised into four domains reflecting different levels of influence within consensus development: steering-group and design-level biases, panel composition and contextual biases, social influence and conformity biases; and individual cognitive heuristic biases. A conceptual framework was developed to systematically identify these biases within Delphi-based consensus studies. Examples illustrating how these biases may arise in healthcare Delphi processes are presented, alongside potential mitigation strategies. Recognition and mitigation of cognitive biases are essential for strengthening the methodological rigour and credibility of Delphi studies. Strategies to reduce bias include diversifying expert panels; using neutral language in survey statements; maintaining anonymity during voting; involving methodological expertise in Delphi design; and ensuring transparent iterative feedback. The framework needs prospective validation before its widespread use and may assist journal editors and peer reviewers in critically appraising Delphi studies and improving reporting standards in consensus research.

papers.abstract: There is an unmet need for repigmentation therapies for patients with nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV) who are candidates for systemic therapy. Here, 52-week primary results are reported from two parallel phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of once-daily povorcitinib (oral, highly selective JAK1 inhibitor) 30 mg in adults with moderate-to-severe NSV (STOP-V1 and STOP-V2). STOP-V1 and STOP-V2 enrolled 467 and 449 patients, respectively. In both studies, the primary endpoint of ≥75% improvement in the facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (F-VASI75) at week 52 was met, demonstrating statistically significant and clinically meaningful repigmentation with povorcitinib versus placebo (STOP-V1: 18.9% versus 6.8%; odds ratio, 3.1; 95% confidence interval 1.6-5.9; P = 0.0003; STOP-V2: 18.9% versus 3.1%; odds ratio, 7.5; 95% confidence interval 3.0-18.6; P < 0.0001). Povorcitinib was well tolerated; the percentage of patients with any treatment-emergent adverse event (TEAE) was similar between the povorcitinib and placebo groups in both studies (STOP-V1/STOP-V2, 68.7%/66.7% versus 63.7%/62.7%). The most common TEAEs with povorcitinib were nasopharyngitis (STOP-V1/STOP-V2, 11.2%/11.3% versus placebo, 9.8%/11.1%), acne (10.7%/10.8% versus 3.0%/2.2%) and upper respiratory tract infection (6.9%/14.0% versus 9.0%/10.7%). Serious TEAEs were generally single events, and Janus kinase inhibitor class-specific TEAEs were absent or rare. These results support once-daily povorcitinib as an effective and well-tolerated systemic treatment for adults with moderate-to-severe NSV. ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers: NCT06113445 , NCT06113471 .

papers.abstract: Readmission after discharge from the intensive care unit (ICU) occurs globally at a rate of approximately 1-12% and is associated with adverse patient outcomes. Despite these findings, there is no internationally accepted tool to guide or standardize decisions regarding ICU discharge. In this scoping review, we aimed to evaluate the use of early warning scores (EWSs) measured at or around the time of ICU discharge as predictors of subsequent ICU readmission in adult and pediatric populations. With support from a medical librarian, we searched MEDLINE®, Embase®, and the Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature from database inception to December 14, 2025. We included quantitative observational and interventional studies that evaluated any EWS (e.g., National EWS [NEWS]/NEWS2, Modified EWS [MEWS], Pediatric EWS [PEWS], Rothman Index, Risk Scoring Index, or related tools) at ICU discharge, immediately prior to transfer, or immediately upon ward admission and reported unplanned ICU readmission following transfer to a hospital ward. Unplanned ICU readmissions were defined as any unplanned return to an ICU after discharge to the ward. We excluded studies in which patients were discharged to locations other than a ward (e.g., home, long-term care) or that focused solely on interfacility transfer. Screening and data extraction were performed in duplicate using a standardized template, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. The search identified 7,977 records, of which 4,824 remained after removal of duplicates. Of the articles, 58 underwent full-text review, and 20 studies met inclusion criteria. The studies were conducted across North America, Europe, and Asia and included both adult (n = 14) and pediatric (n = 6) populations. All were observational (retrospective or prospective) or pre-post intervention designs; no randomized controlled trials were identified. A range of tools were evaluated, including NEWS/NEWS2, MEWS, PEWS, the Rothman Index, the Risk Scoring Index, and several machine-learning-based EWS models. Of the 20 studies, 17 reported a significant association between higher EWS values at or near ICU discharge and increased risk of unplanned ICU readmission, while three found no significant association. Across studies, readmission rates and EWS thresholds varied, and there was considerable heterogeneity in populations, settings, and outcome time frames. The risk of bias was generally low to moderate across QUADAS-2 domains, although several studies had high or unclear risk in key areas-most commonly patient selection and index test blinding-limiting causal inference. Most available studies report that higher EWS values at ICU discharge are associated with an increased likelihood of ICU readmission. Early warning scores may therefore serve as useful adjuncts to clinical judgement when assessing discharge readiness. Nevertheless, the current evidence base is limited by the absence of randomized or robust interventional trials, and substantial heterogeneity, which limits causal inference and the ability to determine whether EWS-guided discharge protocols improve outcomes. Further multicentre prospective studies are needed to determine whether EWS-guided discharge protocols improve patient outcomes, reduce readmissions, and optimize use of ICU resources.

papers.abstract: Glioblastoma invasion into healthy brain tissue remains a major barrier to effective treatment, but the dynamic single-cell behaviors underlying this process remain difficult to measure across patient models. Here, we introduce GlioTrace, an ex vivo imaging and computational framework for real-time tracking of glioblastoma invasion in patient-derived xenograft brain slices. Combining whole-specimen confocal microscopy with machine learning-based morphology classification and probabilistic modeling of state transitions, GlioTrace reconstructs how tumor cells switch between invasion phenotypes and how these dynamics are shaped by local tissue context and therapy. Across six patient-derived models, GlioTrace reveals that invasion plasticity is patient-specific, spatially organized, and modulated by vascular proximity and microglial interaction. Targeted therapies selectively alter phenotype composition and transition probabilities, whereas standard-of-care treatment enriches a highly motile, transition-connected branching state consistent with a treatment-tolerant invasive phenotype. Thus, GlioTrace makes glioblastoma invasion a measurable dynamic process for comparing patient-specific treatment responses in living brain tissue.

papers.abstract: Ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) are distinct diseases but may share fibroblast mediated mechanisms involving tissue remodeling and inflammation. However, their common molecular features at single cell resolution remain insufficiently defined. We integrated single cell RNA sequencing datasets from ICM and LUAD with bulk transcriptomic profiles from TCGA LUAD, GSE18842, and GSE48166. Differential expression analysis identified 36 shared core genes. A total of 127 combinations of machine learning algorithms and feature selection methods were benchmarked to identify six hub genes: KRTCAP3, RUNX2, DBF4B, C11orf80, COL3A1, and ZFP64. UCell, scMetabolism, SCISSOR, Monocle 3, CellChat, scTenifoldNet/scTenifoldKnk, virtual drug screening, and molecular docking were used for functional characterization. Fibroblasts were the dominant cellular source of the six hub genes in both ICM and LUAD. COL3A1 progressively increased along fibroblast pseudotime trajectories. Virtual overexpression and knockout analyses showed convergence on extracellular matrix organization, inflammatory response, and immune regulation. Cell communication analysis identified fibroblasts as major senders of COLLAGEN signaling, with recipient cells shifting from inflammatory monocytes under normal conditions to proliferating macrophages in ICM and tumor cells in LUAD. Molecular docking nominated Digoxin, Ergotamine, and Ledipasvir as candidate RUNX2-binding compounds with favorable predicted docking scores. This study provides a single cell framework linking ICM and LUAD through fibroblast driven extracellular matrix remodeling and inflammation, and identifies potential molecular targets and therapeutic candidates for further validation.

papers.abstract: Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) regulates tumor progression, metastasis and resistance to therapy. EMT encompasses a continuum of tumor states displaying different functions. The precise dialog between the tumor microenvironment and the different EMT states remains poorly understood. Using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of mouse skin tumors, we uncover that different EMT states are associated with different niches. Neutrophils are more abundant in niches associated with hybrid EMT and secreted oncostatin M, which partially activates EMT while sustaining the epithelial program, promoting hybrid EMT states and metastasis formation. Macrophages are more abundant in niches associated with more advanced EMT states, which, together with other stromal cells, express TGFβ1 that promotes the late EMT state. Oncostatin M and TGFβ1 function in a feed-forward manner by creating distinct inflammatory niches to maintain specific EMT states. Together, our results reveal that distinct niches are associated with specific EMT states and that signaling pathways sustain their own niche's identity by recruiting specific myeloid cell populations.

papers.abstract: Black women with breast cancer in the US experience worse survival and lower quality of life. Addressing information needs and providing emotional and social support may improve survivorship experiences. This study evaluated feasibility and acceptability of an intervention to support Black breast cancer patients. English-speaking, Black, female breast cancer survivors diagnosed with stage I-III breast cancer within five years were invited to participate in a six-week group intervention (virtual or in-person). The intervention was adapted from the PAVING the Path to Wellness program based on a prior qualitative study. Primary endpoints were feasibility and acceptability. Exploratory endpoints included unmet information needs and well-being. Exit interviews with a subset of participants described experiences with, and benefits from, the intervention. 20 women with a mean age of 59.1 years (SD 8.2) and predominantly diagnosed at stage I (n = 11; 55%) participated. Most participants (n = 15; 88.3%) reported high levels of satisfaction and that the program provided new information relevant to their needs and helped motivate lifestyle changes. Nearly all participants (n = 15; 88.3%) expressed that it is important for other Black breast cancer survivors to receive a similar intervention. This study demonstrates proof of concept and provides insights into participant preferences. Broader-scale testing is needed to assess generalizability. NCT05700396, Registration Date: 2023-01 -17.

papers.abstract: To characterize the cancer phenotype and clinical presentation across molecularly distinct EPCAM deletion subgroups and determine how the phenotype varies with MSH2 involvement. We retrospectively evaluated 662 unrelated probands undergoing hereditary cancer multigene panel testing (MGPT) with isolated EPCAM full-gene deletions (n = 22), isolated EPCAM 3' deletions (n = 96), contiguous EPCAM full-gene deletions extending into MSH2 (n = 64), contiguous EPCAM 3' deletions extending into MSH2 (n = 116), MSH2 gross deletions (n = 155), and MSH2 nonsense/frameshift (ns/fs) variants (n = 209). Lynch syndrome (LS)-associated cancer prevalence, tumor spectrum, and PREMM5 scores were compared across cohorts. Multivariable logistic regression estimated cancer-specific associations relative to a MGPT-negative reference cohort. Isolated EPCAM full-gene deletions, comprising 18.6% of observed isolated EPCAM deletions, were not significantly associated with LS-associated cancers. The LS-associated cancer prevalence was 13.6% in this cohort, compared with 54.6% with isolated EPCAM 3' deletions and 64.1%-72.2% in MSH2-involving cohorts (P < .001). Relative to MGPT-negative individuals, isolated EPCAM 3' deletions were strongly associated with colorectal cancer (odds ratio [OR], 17.59; P < .001) but not endometrial cancer (OR, 0.76; P = .790). MSH2-involving cohorts demonstrated strong associations with both colorectal (ORs, 8.50-16.03; P < .001) and endometrial cancers (ORs, 17.31-30.47; P < .001). These findings provide new insights into the molecular and clinical heterogeneity of germline deletions involving EPCAM. Expanded detection across the full EPCAM gene and its 3' region distinguishes isolated full-gene deletions, which do not disrupt downstream MSH2 and are not associated with LS phenotypes, from isolated 3' deletions with a colorectal-predominant phenotype, and contiguous EPCAM-MSH2 deletions with an MSH2-like LS phenotype. Precise delineation of EPCAM deletion boundaries and MSH2 involvement define three clinically relevant risk groups and support more precise risk assessment, counseling, and surveillance.

papers.abstract: Local control after Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for radioresistant brain metastases remains variable. Melanoma and renal cell carcinoma brain metastases are relatively radioresistant, yet pre-treatment prediction of local failure and its timing remains limited. We developed and internally validated a survival machine learning model to predict lesion-specific local failure and time to local failure using only pre-GKRS variables. We performed a retrospective single-center study of melanoma and renal cell carcinoma brain metastases treated with GKRS. Local failure was modeled as a right-censored survival outcome. A Random Survival Forest (RSF) was trained using baseline demographic, clinical, and tumor-level variables available before treatment. The individual lesion was the prediction unit, while data partitioning was performed at the patient level to minimize information leakage. Performance was assessed using the concordance index, cumulative/dynamic AUC, and Brier score with patient-grouped 5-fold internal cross-validation. The cohort included 893 lesions, of which 228 (25.5%) developed local failure. In the holdout test set (179 lesions), the RSF achieved a C-index of 0.842. Dynamic AUC values were 0.904, 0.890, and 0.851 at 6, 12, and 24 months, respectively, with corresponding Brier scores of 0.130, 0.153, and 0.152. Cross-validation demonstrated stable performance, with a mean C-index of 0.882. The strongest predictors were age at treatment, pre-treatment KPS, and tumor volume. Pre-treatment RSF modeling demonstrated strong internal performance for predicting local failure and time to local failure after GKRS in radioresistant brain metastases, supporting its potential for individualized risk stratification and follow-up planning. Not applicable.

papers.abstract: Breast cancer surgery is generally considered to be low risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, when VTE occurs, it may lead to severe complications and increased mortality. This study aimed to determine the incidence, predictors, and clinical impact of postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery using a large, multicenter surgical database. The American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database (2008-2023) was queried to identify female patients undergoing surgery for breast cancer without concurrent reconstruction. Patients were stratified according to postoperative VTE occurrence. Demographics, comorbidities, laboratory values, operative characteristics, and 30-day outcomes were compared. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of VTE and to construct a predictive model, which was internally validated using bootstrap resampling. Among 270,564 patients included, 465 (0.2%) developed postoperative VTE. Of these, 247 (53.1%) had deep vein thrombosis, 177 (38.1%) pulmonary embolism, and 41 (8.8%) both. Patients who developed VTE were older, had higher body mass index (BMI), greater comorbidity burden, and longer operative times (all p < 0.001). They also demonstrated lower preoperative serum albumin, hematocrit, prothrombin time, and albumin-to-creatinine ratio. VTE was associated with significantly longer hospital stays, increased rates of reoperation and readmission, and a more than 20-fold higher crude 30-day mortality (1.9% vs. 0.1%) (all p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, increasing age (OR 1.26 per 10 years), BMI (OR 1.17 per 5 kg/m²), congestive heart failure (OR 2.43), metastatic cancer (OR 2.05), lower serum albumin (OR 0.63 per 1 g/dL), and longer operative duration (OR 1.09 per 30 min) were independently associated with postoperative VTE. Compared with partial mastectomy, total mastectomy (OR 2.58), modified radical mastectomy (OR 2.22), and radical mastectomy (OR 2.80) were associated with significantly higher odds of postoperative VTE. The predictive model demonstrated acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.717; optimism-corrected 0.700) and good calibration. Age, BMI, congestive heart failure, metastatic cancer, mastectomy and operative time remained associated with VTE in all sensitivity analyses. Postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery is uncommon but associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Advanced age, obesity, cardiac comorbidity, metastatic disease, hypoalbuminemia, longer operative duration, and greater surgical extent were independently associated with increased thromboembolic risk. Awareness of these risk factors may support individualized perioperative risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis decisions, as recommended by current consensus guidance, and facilitate earlier recognition of postoperative VTE.
